subject.title: Bound HTTP error body snippets to readable streams

question: May this PR intentionally drop diagnostic body text for shipped body-less or non-readable Response adapters, or must OpenClaw preserve a bounded diagnostic path for those adapters?
rationale: Whole-body methods cannot enforce the existing byte cap, but returning an empty snippet removes previously tested and shipped diagnostic behavior; repository policy treats fallback removal and fail-closed changes as compatibility-sensitive.

options.title: Approve fail-closed fallback
options.body: Accept empty snippets when no cancellable reader exists, with caller-level regression coverage and real runtime proof before merge.

options.title: Add a bounded adapter contract
options.body: Preserve diagnostics only through a new explicitly bounded reader seam rather than calling `text()` or `arrayBuffer()` on arbitrary responses.

recommendation.title: Approve fail-closed fallback
recommendation.body: Accept empty snippets when no cancellable reader exists, with caller-level regression coverage and real runtime proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent work on bounding external-provider HTTP responses most directly overlaps the memory-safety invariant and diagnostic tradeoff here.
